region: Namib dunes, Skeleton Coast, Damaraland and Etosha
title: Namibia — Dunes, Fog Coast and Etosha by Rooftop Tent
subtitle: A 14-day self-drive loop from Windhoek through the Namib, the Atlantic coast, Damaraland and the green-season pans of Etosha
summary: A 12-day 4x4 loop of about 2,900 km with rooftop-tent camping: Sossusvlei, Swakopmund, Spitzkoppe, Twyfelfontein and Etosha, driven by the group itself. Spectacular and independent, but the single 4x4 hire makes it expensive.
introduction: Twelve days in one rooftop-tent Land Cruiser, starting at the Windhoek rental yard. The route climbs over Spreetshoogte Pass to Sesriem for sunrise on Dune 45 and the dead trees of Deadvlei, drops to the fog-bound Atlantic at Swakopmund and Cape Cross, then turns inland to the granite domes of Spitzkoppe. Damaraland brings Twyfelfontein's rock engravings and the search for desert-adapted elephants; Etosha closes the loop with three nights at waterhole camps. Almost every night is a campsite, mostly gravel roads connect them, and the rains of February and March turn the dry riverbeds into a real planning variable.

exceptional.vsOman: Oman combined mountain and desert camping in one compact country; Namibia is longer-range and wilder, with 2,900 km, far fewer people and a rooftop tent instead of ground tents. Gravel driving is more constant, and wildlife (Etosha, desert elephants) adds a dimension Oman did not have.
exceptional.vsPackageTourism: Package tours run a fixed lodge-to-lodge circuit in a guided minibus. Here the group drives itself, sleeps at NWR and community campsites, chooses when to wait for light at Dune 45 and decides how long to sit at a waterhole.
exceptional.vsPortfolio: Namibia is the only destination in the portfolio built around self-drive desert driving combined with big-game viewing, and it pairs the Namib Sand Sea with an Atlantic fog coast and a cold-water seal colony within one loop.

duration.note: Overnight flights on day 1 (arrive day 2) and day 13 (arrive day 14); the vehicle is hired for 12 days (day 2 to day 13).

recommendedTravelWindow.rationale: March is later in the rains, so grass is still green but pans begin to dry, roads recover and animals start to return to the waterholes; February is the wettest, hottest month. The window avoids Independence Day (21 March) and the Easter 2027 holidays (Easter is 28 March), when campsites fill.

februarySuitability.summary: Hottest and wettest month: 35 C or more at Sesriem, flooded riverbeds in the north and animals dispersed in Etosha. Good for newborn animals and birds and lowest vehicle rates, but gravel roads can close.

marchSuitability.summary: Slightly cooler nights, rains tapering and roads recovering, while Etosha is still green and quiet. Still hot in the desert and gravel-road risk remains. Wildlife viewing improves towards April.

climate.regionNote: Inland Namib/Sesriem (hot desert), Atlantic coast at Swakopmund/Walvis Bay (cool, foggy), Windhoek plateau and northern Etosha/Damaraland (summer rains). Ranges are typical values from secondary climate sources, not a 2027 forecast.

february.rainfall: Summer rain peaks on the plateau and north (Windhoek roughly 100 mm over about 16 days); the southwest and coast stay close to dry.
february.humidity: Low in the desert, moderate in the north.
february.notes: Coast stays 17–24 C. Thunderstorms can flood dry riverbeds (omuramba) and close gravel roads.

march.rainfall: Rains taper; Windhoek about 11 rain days in March; the north can still be wet.
march.humidity: Low in the desert, moderate in the north.
march.notes: Etosha pans start to dry; roads begin to recover. Desert heat remains severe by midday.

climate.snowAndMountainAccess: Not relevant: no snow; Spreetshoogte Pass is steep gravel but open all year except after heavy rain.
climate.seaConditions: Atlantic water is cold (about 13–16 C); fog on the coast; heavy swell makes swimming unsuitable.
climate.airQuality: Good; dust on gravel roads and sandstorms are possible.
climate.wildlifeSeasonality: Green season: births, birds and migrant waders, but game is dispersed in Etosha and viewing is harder than in the dry season (S15). Permanent waterholes remain reliable.

holidaysAndFestivals.name: Namibian Independence Day
holidaysAndFestivals.impact: Public holiday; busy campsites and shops closed around it; the proposed window ends before.

holidaysAndFestivals.name: Easter 2027
holidaysAndFestivals.dates: Good Friday 26 March, Easter Sunday 28 March 2027
holidaysAndFestivals.impact: Namibian school and tourist peak; avoid by travelling earlier in March.

climate.ramadan2027: Not relevant: Muslim population is small and tourism services are unaffected.
climate.tourismDemand: Low season (green season): lower rental rates, fewer visitors, lodges and camps generally available, but NWR sites should still be booked.
climate.flightPriceSeasonality: February–March 2027 Paris–Windhoek return fares of about EUR 776–826 were seen as statistics (S14); the peak season is July–October.

geography.summary: A transect from the dune sea of the Namib across the Atlantic fog coast to granite inselbergs, sandstone river valleys and the salt-pan savanna of Etosha.
geography.distinctive: The Namib Sand Sea (UNESCO-listed in 2013) has some of the tallest star dunes on Earth, and the cold Benguela Current creates a fog coast where desert meets ocean at Sandwich Harbour.

landscapes.name: Sossusvlei and Deadvlei
landscapes.description: Red star dunes up to about 300 m high around a white clay pan studded with dead camel thorn trees.

landscapes.name: Skeleton Coast and Cape Cross
landscapes.description: Cold Atlantic coast with fog, wrecks and a Cape fur seal colony.

landscapes.name: Spitzkoppe
landscapes.description: Granite inselbergs and a natural rock arch rising from the plain.

landscapes.name: Etosha Pan
landscapes.description: A salt pan of about 4,800 km2 edged by mopane woodland and permanent waterholes.

culture.summary: Depth comes from San rock art at Twyfelfontein and Spitzkoppe and German colonial history on the coast, including the 1904–08 genocide of Herero and Nama people. Himba culture is deliberately not scheduled as a stop; see the research note.

culturalHighlights.name: Twyfelfontein rock engravings
culturalHighlights.description: A UNESCO-listed site with about 2,500 engravings made by hunter-gatherers; visits are with community guides, which keeps income local.

culturalHighlights.name: Bushman's Paradise, Spitzkoppe
culturalHighlights.description: San rock paintings on granite; reached on foot with a community guide from the community campsite.

culturalHighlights.name: Swakopmund and Windhoek colonial history
culturalHighlights.description: German colonial architecture, with museums that also cover the colonial wars and independence in 1990.

culturalHighlights.name: Namutoni fort
culturalHighlights.description: A 1905 German fort that doubles as an Etosha camp.

adventureHighlights.name: Self-drive gravel and sand driving
adventureHighlights.description: About 2,900 km, most of it on gravel and some in deep sand at Sossusvlei. Needs a tyre-pressure routine, a compressor and slow speeds (80 km/h maximum).

adventureHighlights.name: Dune 45 and Big Daddy at dawn
adventureHighlights.description: Dune climbs before the heat; start at sunrise and carry water.

adventureHighlights.name: Sandwich Harbour dune-and-lagoon tour
adventureHighlights.description: Tide-dependent 4x4 driving where dunes meet the ocean, done with a local operator.

signatureExperiences.title: Dawn at Dune 45 and Deadvlei
signatureExperiences.description: Be at the Sesriem inner gate at sunrise, climb Dune 45 and walk to Deadvlei before the sand heats up.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: Camel-thorn skeletons on a white pan under red dunes.
signatureExperiences.location: Sesriem and Sossusvlei, Namib-Naukluft National Park
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Camp at Sesriem so the inner gate opens earlier; own 4x4 for the last 5 km of sand or walk.
signatureExperiences.costNote: Campsite and park fees; included in the budget lines.

signatureExperiences.title: Sandwich Harbour by local 4x4
signatureExperiences.description: A half-day tide-timed tour where the Namib dunes meet the Atlantic lagoon.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: Few places let you stand on dunes that drop straight into the sea.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Book a local operator for the morning of day 6; the group's rental normally forbids driving the beach.
signatureExperiences.costNote: Planning estimate; operator prices not verified.

signatureExperiences.title: Camping among the boulders at Spitzkoppe
signatureExperiences.description: A community-run campsite beneath granite domes with sunset at the Rock Arch.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: Wild-feeling camping and San rock paintings in a community-managed landscape.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Own 4x4; book the community campsite beforehand if possible.

signatureExperiences.title: Twyfelfontein engravings and the desert elephants
signatureExperiences.description: Guided rock-art walk, then a community-guided search for desert-adapted elephants along the dry Aba-Huab and Huab rivers.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: Elephants adapted to a desert, found along dry rivers.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Stay at a community campsite and arrange guides locally; sightings are not guaranteed.

signatureExperiences.title: Etosha waterhole camps in the green season
signatureExperiences.description: Three nights at Okaukuejo, Halali and Namutoni with floodlit waterholes.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: Quiet, lush Etosha with newborn animals, but dispersed game.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Book NWR camps by email in advance; drive the waterhole circuits slowly.
signatureExperiences.costNote: Camp and park fees are in the budget lines.

travelStyle.summary: A single 4x4 with rooftop tents, shared driving and nine camping nights, plus two guesthouse nights on the coast.

transport.summary: Own rented 4x4 for almost the whole trip; there is no useful public transport for this route.

modes.description: A Land Cruiser or Hilux double cab with two rooftop tents, fridge, spare tyres and camping kit; about 2,900 km on gravel and tar.
A local guided tour for tide-dependent beach and dune driving.

transport.carRental: 4x4 camping companies at Windhoek include Namibia Tours & Safaris and Namib Trails. A four-person Land Cruiser is quoted at N$3,450/day for 1–14 days from January to March 2027 (S07). Standard excess is N$130,000; reduced excess N$535/day and zero excess N$805/day. One-way rental is an optional extra and is not needed for a Windhoek loop. Minimum age and deposit not confirmed. Rental contracts commonly exclude single-vehicle accidents unless the excess option is taken (S02).

drivingRequirements.summary: Self-drive is the standard way to travel in Namibia, on left-hand traffic with paved main roads and long gravel C- and D-roads. Rollovers on gravel are the main tourist risk.
drivingRequirements.internationalDrivingPermit: Not verified from the sources fetched; a French card licence is normally accepted for rental, but check with the rental company whether an international driving permit is required and carry one if they ask.
drivingRequirements.licenceNotes: Two of the four travellers hold car licences and share the driving; the rental contract must list both as additional drivers. A day of 6 hours on gravel should be split between them.
drivingRequirements.motorcycleNotes: No motorcycle riding is proposed; the two travellers without licences ride as passengers.
drivingRequirements.recommendedApproach: Keep to 80 km/h or lower on gravel (S01, S02), lower tyre pressures for sand, avoid driving after dark because of animals, carry two spare tyres and plenty of water, check road reports for flooded riverbeds in Feb–March, and buy the reduced-excess option.

accommodation.summary: Mostly camping at NWR and community campsites, with two guesthouse nights at Swakopmund.
types: Rooftop tent at NWR campsites (Sesriem, Etosha)

camping.summary: Camping is the standard way to travel here and the rental comes equipped; wild camping is prohibited (S01), so stay in designated campsites.

physicalDifficulty.label: demanding
physicalDifficulty.summary: The effort is mostly long gravel driving days, heat of 35 C or more and dune climbing; no technical skills are needed, but fatigue management is.

itinerary.summary: A 14-day loop: Windhoek, Sesriem, Swakopmund, Spitzkoppe, Twyfelfontein, Etosha and back, with a 12-day vehicle rental and two flexible days (day 6 and day 9, plus a day-12 buffer).

days.title: Overnight to Namibia
activities: Fly CDG–Frankfurt, then the overnight flight to Windhoek
days.transport: Flights CDG–FRA–WDH (Lufthansa group; Discover Airlines flies FRA–WDH, not verified for March 2027)
days.practical: Book flights as one ticket so the connection is protected; keep one carry-on with warm layers and the 4x4 rental voucher.

days.title: Arrive, collect the 4x4, stock up
activities: Collect the 4x4 and check spare tyres, compressor, tent, fridge and recovery kit with the rental company
Shop in Windhoek (food for several days and 20 L of water per person)
Change money or withdraw N$ from an ATM inside a bank or mall
Early night at a Windhoek campsite
days.travelTime: ≈ 45 min airport to town; free afternoon
days.culturalHighlight: Christuskirche and the Independence Memorial Museum if energy allows
days.practical: Photograph every dent at pick-up; ask the company whether it covers tyres, windscreens and single-vehicle accidents (S02). Do not walk around at night.

days.title: Over the Spreetshoogte Pass to the Namib
activities: Drive the C26 over Spreetshoogte Pass (steep, gravel, 9 km descent)
Fuel at Solitaire or earlier; arrive Sesriem for sunset
Optional sunset drive to Elim Dune
days.geographicalHighlight: Edge of the Namib; escarpment views
days.practical: Fill the tank in Windhoek and re-check both spare tyres; Sesriem inner gate lets campers into the park before the main gate.

days.title: Dune 45, Deadvlei and Sesriem Canyon
activities: Sunrise at Dune 45 (45 km from gate)
Drive to the 2x4 parking, walk or take the 4x4 track to Deadvlei and Sossusvlei
Retreat to camp during the heat peak (shade, cold drinks)
Late-afternoon walk through Sesriem Canyon
days.transport: Own 4x4 (last 5 km deep sand, lower tyre pressure)
days.geographicalHighlight: Star dunes and clay pan; heat of 35 C or more by mid-morning, so start before sunrise
days.practical: Carry 4 L of water each; Feb–March midday sand temperature is dangerous; gate times follow sunrise (S10).

days.title: Solitaire, Kuiseb Pass and the cold coast
activities: Gravel via Solitaire and the Kuiseb and Gaub passes
Welwitschia and moon-landscape stops if time
Evening at the Walvis Bay lagoon, then check in to a Swakopmund guesthouse
days.geographicalHighlight: Transition from dune desert to fog coast
days.practical: The longest gravel day: start by 7:30 and be off gravel by about 15:00; check river crossings and road reports for flooded riverbeds.

days.title: Sandwich Harbour and the town
activities: Morning guided 4x4 tour to Sandwich Harbour with a local operator
Walvis Bay lagoon at low-tide for birds
Afternoon rest and laundry; seafood dinner
days.transport: Operator's 4x4 for the dune section; own vehicle in town
days.practical: Tour times depend on the tide, book once the trip dates are fixed; the group's rental contract normally forbids driving the beach.

days.title: Seals on the Skeleton Coast, granite at Spitzkoppe
activities: Drive the C34 salt road to Cape Cross seal colony
Turn inland via Henties Bay to Spitzkoppe
Sunset at the Rock Arch, camp among the boulders
days.culturalHighlight: Rock paintings at Bushman's Paradise with a community guide
days.geographicalHighlight: Granite inselbergs on a flat plain
days.practical: Fill up in Swakopmund; no fuel at Spitzkoppe.

days.title: Inland to Damaraland
activities: Gravel through Uis and the Brandberg area
Afternoon arrival at a community-run campsite near Twyfelfontein
Short walk at sunset
days.practical: Check recent rain on the D2612; rainy-season flash floods can cut the riverbeds. Fill fuel in Uis.

days.title: Rock art and the desert-adapted elephants
activities: Guided walk among the engravings (guiding is mandatory and supports the community)
Organ Pipes and Burnt Mountain
Optional guided 4x4 search for desert-adapted elephants with community guides
days.culturalHighlight: Rock engravings on UNESCO's World Heritage list
days.geographicalHighlight: Sandstone and basalt hills along dry rivers
days.practical: Flexible rest day: elephant sightings are not guaranteed in the green season when they range widely; do not approach the animals.

days.title: To Etosha
activities: Gravel D2612 to Khorixas, then tarred road via Kamanjab to Anderson Gate
Arrive Okaukuejo before dusk; sit at the waterhole after dark
days.practical: Etosha camps are reserved ahead via NWR; gates close at sunset, so leave early.

days.title: Etosha waterhole circuit
activities: Drive the pan-edge road and visit the permanent waterholes (Okaukuejo, Gemsbokvlakte, Halali, Rietfontein, Goas)
Night waterhole vigil at Halali
days.travelTime: Park roads, ≈ 5–6 h over the day
days.practical: Expect dispersed animals in Feb–March; permanent waterholes are the reliable places (S15).

days.title: Eastern Etosha
activities: Drive to Namutoni via Fisher's Pan
Climb the fort tower at sunset
days.practical: Second flexible buffer: if flights leave later than day 13 evening, take a slower morning and drive on day 13 afternoon.

days.title: Drive south and return the 4x4
activities: Leave via Von Lindequist Gate at opening
Tarred B1 via Tsumeb, Otjiwarongo and Okahandja to Windhoek
Return the vehicle in the afternoon and transfer to the airport for the night flight
days.practical: Ask the rental company for a late drop-off at the airport; keep 3 h margin before the flight. Departure time for March 2027 is not verified.

days.title: Home
activities: Arrive Frankfurt in the morning, connect to Paris CDG
days.practical: Declare no wildlife products: buying or transporting protected wildlife items is illegal (S02).

stops.name: Hosea Kutako International Airport (WDH)
stops.description: International gateway 45 km east of Windhoek; arrival and departure.
stops.transport: Taxi or rental-company transfer to Windhoek.

stops.name: Windhoek
stops.description: Capital and vehicle pick-up/return; first-night campsite, supermarkets (Spar, Checkers), cash, SIM card and German-colonial/independence-era sights.
activities: Collect and check the 4x4
Shop for 12 days of food and water
Christuskirche and Independence Museum if time
stops.culturalImportance: Heart of colonial German and independence-era history; Herero and Nama heritage museums.
stops.transport: Rental 4x4; walk in the centre by day, avoid walking at night.

stops.name: Sesriem (Namib-Naukluft gateway)
stops.description: Gateway to Sossusvlei; NWR campsite with sites under camel thorn trees; Sesriem Canyon is 4 km away.
activities: Sesriem Canyon walk
Sunset at Elim Dune
stops.geography: Edge of the Namib Sand Sea, UNESCO-listed in 2013.
stops.transport: Own 4x4; gravel C-roads from Windhoek via Spreetshoogte Pass.

stops.name: Sossusvlei and Deadvlei
stops.description: Dune 45, Big Daddy, Deadvlei clay pan and Sossusvlei, 65 km from the Sesriem gate on a paved road, then 5 km of deep sand (4x4 or shuttle).
activities: Sunrise at Dune 45
Walk to Deadvlei
Optional climb of Big Daddy
stops.geography: Star dunes up to c. 300 m; camel thorn skeletons.
stops.transport: Own 4x4 only on last 5 km; sand driving requires lowered tyre pressure and a compressor.

stops.name: Solitaire
stops.description: Fuel and bakery stop between Sesriem and the Kuiseb Pass; last reliable fuel for about 250 km.
activities: Fuel, pastries, rest

stops.name: Walvis Bay lagoon
stops.description: Ramsar-listed lagoon with flamingos and pelicans; starting point for Sandwich Harbour tours.
activities: Lagoon birdwatching
Sandwich Harbour half-day 4x4 tour with a local operator
stops.geography: Cold Benguela coast, fog and dunes.
stops.transport: Tarred road from Walvis Bay to Swakopmund.

stops.name: Swakopmund
stops.description: Coastal town with German colonial architecture and fresh seafood; cool, foggy coast (17–24 C in February) after the desert heat.
activities: Jetty and old town walk
Seafood dinner
Laundry, supplies and fuel
stops.culturalImportance: German colonial-era architecture and the legacy of the 1904–1908 colonial wars (Herero and Nama genocide) are documented in local museums.
stops.accommodation: Guesthouse, two twin rooms, N$1,500 per room (estimate)

stops.name: Cape Cross Seal Reserve
stops.description: Colony of Cape fur seals on the Skeleton Coast road, 120 km north of Swakopmund; Diego Cao's 1486 cross replica nearby.
activities: Walk the seal viewing boardwalk
Skeleton Coast salt road
stops.culturalImportance: Portuguese navigator Diogo Cao landed here in 1486.

stops.name: Spitzkoppe Community Campsite
stops.description: Granite inselbergs ('Matterhorn of Namibia') and rock arch; community-run campsite among boulders; San rock paintings at Bushman's Paradise.
activities: Sunset at the Rock Arch
Walk to rock paintings with a community guide
stops.geography: Granite inselbergs rising c. 700 m above the plain.
stops.accommodation: Community campsite, c. N$300 per person (estimate)
stops.costNote: Per person per night incl. entry (estimate)

stops.name: Twyfelfontein / Damaraland
stops.description: UNESCO-listed rock engravings, Organ Pipes, Burnt Mountain and a community-run campsite; desert-adapted elephants in the Aba-Huab and Huab riverbeds.
activities: Guided engravings walk
Organ Pipes
Guided desert-elephant search with community guides
stops.culturalImportance: One of the largest concentrations of rock art in Africa, with c. 2,500 engravings (UNESCO).
stops.geography: Dry river valleys between sandstone and basalt.
stops.transport: Own 4x4 on gravel D2612 and D3254.
stops.accommodation: Community campsite near Twyfelfontein, c. N$300 per person (estimate)

stops.name: Okaukuejo (Etosha)
stops.description: Etosha's main western camp with a floodlit waterhole; Anderson Gate is 17 km away.
activities: Waterhole watching at dusk and dawn
Self-drive loops along the pan edge
stops.geography: Etosha Pan, a 4,800 km2 salt pan; savanna and mopane woodland.
stops.transport: Own 4x4 on tarred and gravel park roads; speed limit 60 km/h.

stops.name: Halali (Etosha)
stops.description: Central Etosha camp with a rocky-hill waterhole (Moringa, Rietfontein, Goas nearby).
activities: Waterhole circuits
Night waterhole wait
stops.geography: Dolomite hill on the pan edge.

stops.name: Namutoni (Etosha)
stops.description: Eastern camp in a white 1905 German fort with Fisher's Pan nearby.
activities: Fort lookout at sunset
Fisher's Pan flamingos and waders if wet

stops.transport: Own 4x4; exit via Von Lindequist Gate.

route.routingNote: Connections are schematic straight lines between stops, not verified road geometry.

flights.methodology: Reference departure Paris CDG; return economy fare per person for travel in March 2027, with one stop in Frankfurt or Johannesburg; February snapshot fares used as the base.
flights.airlinesOrSource: Lufthansa group via Frankfurt (S14); Discover Airlines, Air France/KLM, Ethiopian via other hubs were not verified.
flights.baggage: Lowest fares may exclude a checked bag; one bag is priced separately in the baggage line.
flights.priceNote: Representative figures from fare statistics for Feb 2027 (about EUR 776–826); March 2027 fares were not yet on sale when checked. Not a live quote.

alternatives.note: Frankfurt is the main hub; this is a planning guess without a quote.

lines.label: One checked bag per person, return
lines.note: Light economy fares often exclude a checked bag; estimate.

lines.label: 4x4 double cab with 2 rooftop tents and camping kit for 4
lines.note: Realistic: N$3,450/day (Jan–Mar 2027, 1–14 days) / 18.9949 = EUR 181.6. Economical assumes about N$2,900/day from a cheaper operator (estimate). Comfortable: higher-season-level N$4,400/day. One-way fee not applicable (return in Windhoek).

lines.label: Reduced-excess cover (N$535/day)
lines.note: Standard cover leaves an excess of N$130,000 (about EUR 6,840), so the realistic plan buys reduced excess (N$535/day = EUR 28.2). Economical keeps the standard cover (EUR 0 extra) and accepts the excess; comfortable buys zero excess (N$805/day = EUR 42.4).

lines.label: Diesel for about 2,900 km
lines.note: About 14.8 L/100 km for a loaded Land Cruiser on gravel; diesel about N$27.9/l (EUR 1.47) in late 2026; fuel in March 2027 not known.

lines.label: Guarded parking and tips (no tolls on this route)
lines.note: Namibia has no tolls on this route; the line is for informal car-guards in Windhoek and Swakopmund.

lines.label: No private driver; Sandwich Harbour tour is under activities
Swakopmund guesthouse, 2 twin rooms, 2 nights
lines.note: N$1,500 per twin room for realistic (EUR 79). Not verified for March 2027.

lines.label: 9 camping nights (Windhoek, Sesriem x2, Spitzkoppe, Twyfelfontein x2, Etosha x3)
lines.note: Sesriem N$670 pp (S09); other sites are planning estimates of N$250–600 pp (Etosha NWR rate not confirmed). Average about EUR 25–26 per person-night.

lines.label: Fridge and extras beyond the rental camping kit
lines.note: Namib Trails charges N$90/day for an Engel fridge (EUR 4.7); a basic cooler box is included in the rental.

lines.label: Supermarket food, braai, some restaurants
lines.note: Self-catering from Spar/Checkers with seafood and restaurants in Swakopmund.

lines.label: Bottled/refill water
lines.note: Tap water is drinkable in towns; carry 4 L per person per day in the desert.

lines.label: Park and site fees (Etosha 3 days, Sossusvlei 2, Twyfelfontein, Cape Cross, Spitzkoppe)
lines.note: NWR park-entrance PDF could not be opened, so fees are a planning estimate (about N$2,500 per person incl. vehicle share); confirm before booking.

lines.label: Sandwich Harbour guided half-day 4x4 tour
lines.note: Operator prices not verified; economical swaps for a cheaper small-group tour.

lines.label: Community guides (Twyfelfontein, Spitzkoppe, elephant search)
lines.note: Site guiding at Twyfelfontein is paid at the gate; the figure also covers tips.

lines.label: Namibia visa on arrival or e-visa
lines.note: NAD 1,600 / 18.9949 = EUR 84.2 (FCDO S04). One French-language source mentions an extra NAD 400 service fee for visa-on-arrival, unconfirmed; the comfortable scenario includes it.

lines.note: Park fees are in the entrance-fee line. A Kolmanskop/Lüderitz diamond-area permit is not needed because that area is not on the route.

lines.label: Travel insurance with medical evacuation and rental-vehicle excess cover
lines.note: Choose a policy covering repatriation and gravel driving; remote Damaraland/Etosha medical access is limited (S03, S06).

budget.exceptionalJustification: The realistic total is above the EUR 2,500 ceiling, so it is informational only. About EUR 630 per person is the 12-day four-person 4x4 with reduced-excess insurance, and fuel for 2,900 km adds about EUR 158; a credible cheaper variant (central Namib loop, 8 vehicle days) is described in the research note and still lands near EUR 2,500.

scenarioNotes.economical: A cheaper rental operator with standard-excess cover, fewer extras and cheaper food; the lowest credible price and riskier because the excess is N$130,000.
scenarioNotes.realistic: One 4x4 Land Cruiser with reduced-excess cover, 9 camping nights and 2 guesthouse nights; the headline.
scenarioNotes.comfortable: Zero-excess cover, higher rental rate, more guesthouse-level comfort, and a higher flight fare.

security.summary: Namibia is politically stable. Official advice reviewed shows no regions against travel on the route; the main risks are road accidents on gravel, urban crime in Windhoek, wildlife and rainy-season flooding. The Netherlands rates it yellow; France's colour map could not be read from the page text.
security.assessedRoute: Windhoek, Sesriem/Sossusvlei, Walvis Bay/Swakopmund, Cape Cross, Spitzkoppe, Twyfelfontein, Etosha and return via the B1. The Zambezi (Caprivi) region, Angolan border and the Lüderitz diamond restricted area are not on the route.

advisories.level: No regional ban in the advice text; the colour of the security map (updated 11 March 2026) could not be read from the fetched text; general alert 'Vigilance renforcée' of 10 Sept 2026 does not name Namibia in the text seen.
advisories.regionsAffected: Windhoek and cities (crime); Diamond Restricted Area between Lüderitz and Oranjemund; Angola border strips.
advisories.routeImpact: None of the flagged areas is on the route; avoid night driving.

advisories.level: No 'against travel' warning found; no regions listed (page updated 10 Dec 2025, current at 28 Nov 2026).
advisories.regionsAffected: None listed; Windhoek crime and gravel-road accidents highlighted.
advisories.routeImpact: No restrictions; road and insurance advice applies.

advisories.level: Yellow (geel); updated 1 Oct 2026, valid until 28 Nov 2026
advisories.regionsAffected: Northern Namibia for flooding (Jan–April); city centres for crime.
advisories.routeImpact: Flooding can affect the northern Etosha/Damaraland roads in Feb–March.

conflictRisk.note: No armed conflict; stable political situation (S01).

terrorismRisk.note: No significant terrorism risk found in the pages reviewed.

kidnappingRisk.note: No kidnapping risk flagged in the pages reviewed.

regionalRestrictions: Diamond Restricted Area (Lüderitz to Oranjemund) is not on the route.
Angola border markings are unclear: stay on the route.
ordinaryRisks: Gravel-road rollovers and tyre blowouts, the main tourist risk (S01, S02)
Wildlife and livestock on roads, especially at night
Muggings, knife attacks and car-park theft in Windhoek (S01, S02)
Flash floods in riverbeds and rainy-season road damage (S02, S03)
Heat of 35 C or more, dehydration and dune fatigue
Malaria risk in northern Etosha in the rainy season (check TravelHealthPro; not verified here)
security.medicalAccess: Windhoek has good private hospitals; hospitals may require payment up front, and Etosha and Damaraland are many hours from care (S06).
security.insuranceConsiderations: Insurance must cover medical evacuation; rental policies often exclude single-vehicle gravel accidents unless the reduced-excess option is taken (S02).
security.reassessmentRequired: Re-check all advisories (especially the France security map colour, which could not be read here, Smartraveller and the US State Department, which were not retrieved) before booking and two weeks before departure; re-check road and flooding conditions and malaria guidance before departure.

practicalRequirements.visa: French citizens need a visa since 1 April 2025, obtainable on arrival at Windhoek/Walvis Bay airports or online as an e-visa; the fee is NAD 1,600 (about EUR 84). Other nationalities must check separately.
practicalRequirements.entry: Entry through Windhoek (WDH) airport; passport must be valid 6 months after arrival with 3 blank pages; yellow fever certificate only if arriving from a risk country (S04, S05).
practicalRequirements.passportValidity: At least 6 months after arrival, with 3 blank pages.
permits: Park entry is paid at gates; Etosha camps are booked through NWR (reservations@nwr.com.na).
No special permits are needed for this route.
practicalRequirements.insurance: Travel insurance with medical evacuation and rental-vehicle excess cover.
practicalRequirements.connectivity: Local SIM available in Windhoek and Swakopmund; coverage drops in the Namib and Damaraland, so download offline maps.
practicalRequirements.payments: Cards accepted in towns and fuel stations; carry some N$ cash for community campsites and guides; watch for card skimming (S02).
practicalRequirements.medical: Consult a travel clinic about malaria prophylaxis for northern Etosha and routine vaccines; carry a first-aid kit.
practicalRequirements.fuel: Fill at every major town; stretches of 250+ km exist (Solitaire, Uis and Etosha camp pumps; fuel at Etosha camps may be unreliable).
equipment: Sun protection and 4 L water per person per day

advantages: Independent desert and wildlife driving that suits experienced travellers
Camping is normal, well-supported and cheap compared with lodges
Green season is quiet, with fewer tourists and the lowest rental rates of the year
Compact loop with a very wide variety of landscapes
disadvantages: Rental, insurance and fuel put the realistic total over EUR 2,500 per person
Long gravel days with rollover risk, and only two of the four can drive
February–March is hot, with flood risk in the north and dispersed game in Etosha
Himba and community-led cultural visits are not part of the route
uncertainties: March 2027 flight prices and exact schedules were not yet on sale
Park, NWR campsite and operator rates for 2027 are estimates
Rainy-season flooding could force route changes in Damaraland and northern Etosha
France's security level colour and the US and Australian advisories could not be read
Whether a French licence alone is accepted by the rental company
